system.concept: Toreador dancer-turned-bodyguard to Prince Sara Anne Winder
system.title: Bodyguard to the Prince
system.biography:
Background

A scandalous dancer in her mortal life, Miriam Caravaggio was Embraced by the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.GaCuLGcjZZjf2EO6]{Toreador} elder Solomon Greene, who saw genius in her movement. Her fascination with the kinship between dance and combat turned her into a lethally graceful fighter, earning her small fame among Kindred. When offered a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} or @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.WaQFCEXFzv8YeAgX]{Assamite} bodyguard, Prince Sara Anne Winder chose Miriam instead, and Miriam has since killed two Kuei-jin assassins sent against the Prince.

Roleplaying Hints

For Miriam, every movement is a dance and every fight a performance. She is a consummate professional who can control her growing taste for combat against the Kuei-jin — for now.
system.notes: Sire: Solomon Greene. Disciplines (as printed): Auspex 4, Celerity 4, Fortitude 4, Potence 2, Presence 2, Protean 2, Obfuscate 1.

system.description: Maintain physical contact with an object or location and concentrate for a turn, expending a Mental Trait, then ask the Narrator one question about who last touched it, whether it was involved in stressful situations, or what strong emotions drove its user. May be used repeatedly for greater insight; objects of powerful emotional resonance may force a derangement upon the user for the scene.

By this gift, a Toreador may penetrate the "soul" of an inanimate artwork she examines, interpreting the piece, gleaning the artist's state of mind, the relationship between artist and work, and the stages of the creative process, revealed as a series of progressively paler images looking back into the work's history. Some Toreador use this to critique or authenticate a piece; others monitor their proteges' work for unspoken rebellion or sadness, or seek the "real" story behind a letter proposing an alliance. The power does not function on "living" art still in the act of performance — a play, a song, or a story being told — since such work depends on the performer's ongoing intent rather than a fixed, finished creation.

System: The character examines the work and the number of successes determines how much she perceives: a single success yields only general feelings with no historical context; two successes offer a vague sense of the work's history; three successes reveal specific details and a fuzzy timeline; four successes grant a definite sense of the artist's emotional state and a reasonable timeline; five successes let the Toreador see the work in stages, feeling what the artist felt at every step of its creation. The difficulty rises for pieces with multiple artists or a long creation span; examining something as vast as a cathedral or castle risks leaving the Toreador a gibbering wreck from informational overload.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis II: Keepers of the Word, Book One: Artisans (Toreador)

system.description: By spending a Blood Trait, you gain a further additional action at the end of the turn, on top of any gained from Swiftness.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

system.description:
Assamites who hone both their preternatural senses and their speed learn a valuable secret: sometimes it is wiser to defend than to attack. A vampire with this power enters a brief trance in which she perceives every threat against her at once, assessing and reacting to each in turn.

System: At the start of a combat turn, before actions are declared, the player spends two Blood Traits and a Willpower Trait to activate this power (this counts as activating Celerity for the turn). The character takes no offensive action that turn, but may defend against every attack made against her, contesting each one individually. This power may be used no more than a number of times per scene equal to the character's Perception Trait total.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis III: Wolves at the Door, Book Two: Saracens

system.description: A combination power blending Potence's unnatural strength with Fortitude's supernatural toughness, letting a Cainite brace her whole body against blunt-force impacts: falling, car crashes, explosions, or being struck by very large objects. It does not help against ordinary combat damage (fists, bullets, blades) or against fire, electricity, sunlight, or other energy-based damage — only against impacts affecting the entire body, and only if the character can see the impact coming and brace for it.
system.source: Mexico City by Night, Chapter Five: Storytelling (Unique Abilities)

system.description: When you suffer lethal or bashing damage, you may make a Simple Test (improved by spending a stamina-related Physical Trait) to remove one level of that damage entirely; usable once per attack, and may be combined with Resilience.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

system.description: By hissing and baring your vampiric features in a Social Challenge, you strike terror into a victim who, if defeated, flees and avoids you for the rest of the scene or hour, risking an extra Trait to act against you if cornered.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

vtmlarp.source: San Francisco by Night, Chapter Five: Honored Shen
